workflow.description: Workflow B v2 for the personal instance (issue #797), proven headless with stubs. A plan node (the test author, Mistral on Pi over LiteLLM) reads the spec's Testing Decisions, the test seams, and plans at most 3 vertical slices. Each slice is unrolled: the test author writes ONE failing test at a seam, a test critic from another family (GLM on Pi, not the test author's and not the writer's) looks for implementation-coupled and tautological tests and the finding check keeps only findings with a checkable quote, a failed verdict sends the test back to the test author once, then the writer (DeepSeek on Pi) makes that one test green. After the last slice build, tests, lint and the coverage gate each run through the gate shim and a failing gate goes to a repair node of the writer (repair-1, repair-2, each followed by every gate again), never ends the run; a failing copier still ends it, since it means a report that does not verify. The writer reviews its own change (self-review, along the Standards and Spec axes, never blocking), then the runner's ticket-review stage (generated by critique-block, read-only tripwire, quote check and refute round) reviews it with critics from competitor families on the Standards and Spec axes, accepts, or sends it to the writer once and reviews it again with fresh critics; after the second failed round an Opus escalation node and a manual check pause the run. The final gates run once more after the review and a failure there goes to a manual check. The file holds no loop, so its cost is known before it runs.

nodes.goal: You are the test author. Read the ticket's acceptance criteria in the requirement document, then the spec the ticket names under Parent: its Testing Decisions section lists the test seams, the places where behaviour is tested. Plan at most 3 vertical slices (tracer bullets), each one behaviour of the ticket that crosses a seam end to end, in the order the behaviours depend on each other, and write the plan to slice-plan.json in the worktree as {"slices": [{"behaviour": "...", "seam": "...", "criterion": "..."}]}. Every slice names a seam the spec lists; when the spec lists none, name the one seam you chose and why. Cover every acceptance criterion in as few slices as possible and never plan more than 3. Write no test and no implementation. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the test author, slice 1 of 3, from a different family than the writer. Read slice-plan.json and write ONE failing test, for slice 1's behaviour only, at the seam the slice names (the spec's Testing Decisions), through that seam's public interface, in the repository's own test style. If the plan holds fewer than 1 slices, write nothing and answer ok. A test describes behaviour, never implementation: no assertion on a private function, a call count or an internal field, no expected value copied from the output of the code under test, and no mock of the unit's own collaborators that decides the result. Run the test and see it fail for the right reason before you answer. Write tests only: no implementation, no change to any non-test file, and no test for a later slice. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the test critic for slice 1, from another family than the test author and the writer. Read the ticket's requirement document, slice-plan.json, the spec's Testing Decisions and the test the test author wrote for slice 1 (the git diff against the base branch). Look for tests coupled to the implementation (an assertion on a private function, a call count or an internal field, a mock of the unit's own collaborators, anything a refactor that keeps behaviour would break), for tautological tests (no assertion, a value copied from the output of the code under test, a mock that returns what it asserts, a test that cannot fail) and for tests outside the seams the spec lists. Write your whole answer, one findings document in the critic finding schema (a findings array, each finding with at least one quote evidence item that is copied verbatim from the test or the ticket, and a no_findings_reason when the array is empty; an empty slice 1 has none), to findings/test-critic-1.json in your own worktree, committed. Change no other file. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

Run the pinned gold-band-gate wrapper for the finding check, which runs gold-band-findings check over the test critic's findings files, the diff and the ticket and answer with its exit status as one fenced json block and nothing else.

Run the pinned gold-band-gate verify copier for the finding check, which runs gold-band-findings check over the test critic's findings files, the diff and the ticket and answer with the report it prints as one fenced json block and nothing else.

Read findings-check.json, the report the finding check wrote into the gate report directory, and answer with its actionable count as one fenced json block and nothing else. A hint is never actionable.

You are the test author, back for the revision of slice 1's test. Read findings-check.json: fix only the findings under kept, which each name a quote that exists in the diff or the ticket, and never act on a hint. Change the slice 1 test only, write no implementation, and add nothing the findings do not ask for. The code review at the end reads the revised test with fresh critics. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the writer, slice 1 of 3. Run slice 1's test first and see it fail (red), then write the least change that makes it pass (green), and only then tidy what you just wrote while every test stays green. If slice-plan.json holds fewer than 1 slices, change nothing and answer ok. Change non-test files only, never edit or delete a test, keep the tests of earlier slices passing and add nothing the slice's test and the requirement do not ask for. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the writer, back for repair 1 of 2 after a gate failed. Read gate-output.txt and gate-report.json in the gate report directory of the gate that failed (build, tests, lint or coverage) and fix the cause. Change non-test files only, never edit or delete a test, and add nothing the failure does not ask for; if the failing test itself is wrong, say so in a comment in your change and leave it. The gates run again and fresh critics review the result. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the writer, back for repair 2 of 2 after a gate failed. Read gate-output.txt and gate-report.json in the gate report directory of the gate that failed (build, tests, lint or coverage) and fix the cause. Change non-test files only, never edit or delete a test, and add nothing the failure does not ask for; if the failing test itself is wrong, say so in a comment in your change and leave it. The gates run again and fresh critics review the result. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

You are the escalation judge: the writer's two repairs did not make every gate pass. Read the failing gate's output and report of the last round and the requirement, judge whether the gate or the ticket is at fault, whether the tests are right and what the owner should decide, and state it in plain words in your answer. Change no file. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.
The owner reads the gate escalation judgment and the failing gate's output and rules on the ticket; the review of the change still runs after the owner's answer.
A gate failed after the code review accepted the change: the owner reads the failing gate's output and rules on the ticket. Nothing repairs the change automatically after its review.

You are the writer, reviewing your own change before the other families do, along the two axes of the code review. Standards: does the diff follow this repository's documented coding standards (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, the glossary and the ADRs)? Spec: does it do what the ticket and the spec it names ask, all of it and nothing more? Fix only a clear defect you find, in non-test files, and change nothing when there is none; never edit or delete a test. This review does not block anything: the critics that follow decide. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

Run the pinned gold-band-gate wrapper around `critique prepare --strict` for the stage for the ticket's code review (/review-implementation) and answer with its exit status as one fenced json block and nothing else. The writer is DeepSeek and the test author Mistral: the orchestrator is bound to the writer's family, so the runner drops it from the roster, and the base depth reviews with the Spec and Standards critics of the other families (Gemini and GLM); do not ask for the deep depth, whose critic is the test author's family.
Run the pinned gold-band-gate verify copier for the prepare gate of the ticket's code review (/review-implementation) and answer with the report it prints as one fenced json block and nothing else.

Run the pinned gold-band-gate verify copier for the fan-out gate of the ticket's code review (/review-implementation) and answer with the report it prints as one fenced json block and nothing else.

You are the orchestrator of the ticket's code review (/review-implementation). The runner's fan-out left each critic's findings in its run directory. Check every finding's evidence against the packet, rule on each one, and write the verdicts file beside the runner's files; add nothing the findings do not support. Answer with one fenced json block holding the findings you could not settle on your own and nothing else: an empty list when every finding has a verdict.

Some finding of the ticket's code review (/review-implementation) cannot be settled without the owner: read the open findings document and state the needs-human case in one short paragraph, naming each finding's id, its location and what the owner must decide. Do not write any file; the manual check after your answer is where the owner rules.

The round is accepted when it is 0.

You are the author of the ticket's code review (/review-implementation). Fresh critics review the result next. Answer with one fenced json block holding ok and nothing else.

the ticket's code review (/review-implementation) could not be accepted in two rounds: read the escalation judge's paragraph and state it to the owner. Do not write any file; the manual check after your answer is where the owner decides, and the run ends here whatever the owner decides: no later stage runs on this artifact automatically.
